Traditional Roast Goose

Served at: St. Martin's Day (Martinstag) · Christmas Day

Serves 6-8Prep 30 minCook 3-4 hours

Roast goose is a magnificent centerpiece for festive occasions, deeply rooted in European culinary traditions. It is famously served on St. Martin's Day (Martinstag) in November, marking the end of the agricultural year, and is a grand, celebratory dish for Christmas Day, symbolizing abundance and feasting during the holiday season.

Ingredients

  • 1 whole goose, 10-12 pounds (4.5-5.5 kg)
  • 2 teaspoons (10 g) salt
  • 1 teaspoon (5 g) freshly ground black pepper
  • 2 large tart apples, cored and quartered (e.g., Granny Smith)
  • 2 medium yellow onions, peeled and quartered
  • 4 sprigs fresh marjoram (or 1 teaspoon dried)
  • 4 sprigs fresh sage (or 1 teaspoon dried)
  • 1 cup (240 ml) hot water or chicken broth (for the roasting pan)

Method

  1. Preheat your oven to 325°F (160°C). Remove the giblets and neck from the goose cavity; reserve them for gravy if desired. Pat the goose dry thoroughly with paper towels.
  2. Prick the skin all over with a sharp fork, especially around the fattest parts (breast, thighs), being careful not to pierce the meat. This allows excess fat to render out during cooking.
  3. Season the inside and outside of the goose generously with salt and freshly ground black pepper.
  4. Stuff the goose cavity loosely with the quartered apples, onions, marjoram, and sage. Do not pack tightly, as this can prevent even cooking.
  5. Truss the goose by tying the legs together with kitchen twine and tucking the wing tips under the body. This helps it cook evenly and maintain its shape.
  6. Place the goose, breast-side up, on a rack in a large roasting pan. Pour the hot water or broth into the bottom of the pan.
  7. Roast for 3-4 hours, or until an instant-read thermometer inserted into the thickest part of the thigh (without touching bone) reads 175°F (80°C).
  8. Every 30-45 minutes, carefully remove the pan from the oven and drain the rendered fat into a heatproof container. This fat can be saved for other culinary uses.
  9. For the last 30 minutes of cooking, increase the oven temperature to 400°F (200°C) to crisp the skin, if desired. Watch carefully to prevent burning.
  10. Once cooked, remove the goose from the oven, transfer it to a carving board, and tent loosely with foil. Let it rest for at least 20-30 minutes before carving. This allows the juices to redistribute, resulting in a more tender and flavorful bird.

Tips

  • Rendered goose fat is a culinary treasure! Store it in the refrigerator for roasting potatoes, vegetables, or making rich pastry.
  • Use the pan drippings (after removing excess fat) to make a luxurious gravy. Deglaze the pan with a little wine or broth, thicken with a roux, and season to taste.
  • Serve roast goose with traditional accompaniments such as braised red cabbage, potato dumplings, roasted chestnuts, or cranberry sauce for a truly festive meal.
